title: Prove a one-off job’s environment and result
goal: Observe /bin/sh execution, captured environment/cwd/umask and actual successful or failed result.
challenge: Repair the prepared wrong captured locale in a distinct one-off retry. Preserve the first actual exit1/result, submit C locale and prove actual UID/cwd/umask/file limit/content/exit0 despite a later different display locale. A vanished queue row is insufficient. Use the supplied6s finite body and keep originals.

steps.command: w=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/foundation-at-execution.XXXXXX") && cd "$w" && umask 077; here() { case "$w" in "$HOME"/foundation-at-execution.??????) ;; *) return 19;; esac; test "${w%/*}" = "$HOME" && test -d "$w" && test ! -L "$w" && test "$(realpath -e "$w")" = "$w" && test "$(pwd -P)" = "$w" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a "$w")" = learner:700; }; fresh() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test ! -e "$1" && test ! -L "$1"; }; regular() { here && test "${1%/*}" = "$w" && test -f "$1" && test ! -L "$1" && test "$(stat -c %U:%a:%h "$1")" = learner:600:1; }; jobid() { regular "$1" || return 19; job=$(awk '$1=="job" && $2 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ {print $2}' "$1"); case "$job" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 19;; *) test "$job" -gt 0;; esac; }; here && test "$(df -B1 --output=avail / | tail -1)" -ge 1073741824 && systemctl is-active atd && pwd

steps.command:
here && fresh "$w/job.sh" && cat > job.sh <<'LL_JOB'
#!/bin/sh
umask 077 || exit 90
ulimit -f 8 || exit 91
test ! -e result && test ! -L result || exit 89
set -C || exit 92
{
 /usr/bin/awk '/^Max file size/ {print "file_limit_soft=" $4 " hard=" $5}' /proc/self/limits
 /usr/bin/timeout --kill-after=2s 6s /bin/sh -c 'printf "identity=%s\nuid=%s\ncwd=%s\numask=%s\n" "$(id -un)" "$(id -u)" "$(pwd -P)" "$(umask)"; printf "LANG=%s\nLC_ALL=%s\n" "$LANG" "$LC_ALL"; test "$LANG" = C && test "$LC_ALL" = C && printf "bounded-job-complete\n"'
 rc=$?
 printf 'exit=%s\n' "$rc"
} > result 2>&1
exit "$rc"
LL_JOB
steps.explanation: Enter this short /bin/sh job manually. Its own6s child timeout and4KiB output limit are explicit; sudo/root can override guest limits.
steps.expected: Private fixed job body, explicit environment/status recording.
